items.title: Frank Adams Interview, 1959-01-20
items.q: But now if you hopped on me and give me friends, then we gonna fight... But now about this boy, Poesie, man. Poesie, man. Poesie, man. He was up there, around there, and I was living then... Not far from there.

ctx.x: How were the Irish people in general in your neighborhood? Were they a tough bunch? Oh yeah, it was tough.

They'd always be fighting and drunk amongst themselves and fight with, and they worked right on the river, on the river front, which is. And in the evening, sometime they get half drunk, you pass by later, they didn't know you anymore, nobody else. And unless you had to scrap with them, if you scrap with them and fight them, and then they know you wasn't going to run, then you and them were good friends, and they look around, well that's Adam. He is out pat, oh, what's Adam? All right, pat you on the back and you…
Was that right in the jailhouse? Right in the jailhouse.
